stories.title: Over 70,000 Leaving Cert students to receive exam results
stories.summary: Over 70,000 Leaving Certificate students will receive their exam results later today, with the overall trend showing fewer top marks awarded, as the impacts of grade deflation continue. The results will be available online and from schools from 10am, with the number of candidates at record high levels. Data from the State Examinations Commission (SEC) show that the class of 2026 has been awarded fewer top grades, with the proportion of H1s down by over one-and-a-half percentage points on 2025. Last year, H1s initially accounted for 11.7% of grades, that figure is down to 10.1% for this year.

stories.title: Social media firms need to 'step up to the plate' - TD
stories.summary: Fianna Fail TD for Carlow-Kilkenny Peter "Chap" Cleere has said social media companies need to "step up to the plate" to stop illegal and reckless behaviour being posted on their platforms. It comes as TikTok has been invited to appear before an Oireachtas media committee to address growing concerns over videos which "glorify illegal activity". Committee chair and Labour TD Alan Kelly said today that the fatal crash on the M9 on Sunday and a trend of videos of people driving the wrong way down motorways must be addressed by companies platforming the footage. TikTok has said it is closely monitoring content related to the incident, in which five teenage boys died and four people were seriously injured in a two-car collision on the motorway in Kildare.

stories.title: US national debt exceeds $40 trillion for first time
stories.summary: The US gross national debt has surged past $40 trillion for the first time, government data showed, outstripping earlier forecasts at a pace fuelled in part by President Donald Trump's invalidated tariffs. The uptick in borrowing comes as longer term US obligations linked to social security and healthcare have been growing, while interest payments have climbed as well. Total public debt outstanding stood at $40.05 trillion at the close of business on Tuesday, according to data released yesterday by the US Treasury Department. This stands in contrast to an earlier forecast by the Congressional Budget Office that overall borrowing would hit $39.4 trillion by the end of fiscal year 2026.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill 16 in Kyiv and surrounding region
stories.summary: Russian bombardments killed at least 16 people in Ukraine's capital and surrounding areas overnight, authorities said, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urging a global response to Moscow's "escalation" of the four-year war. Early this morning, rescuers in Kyiv were sifting through the rubble of destroyed buildings, including a damaged children's hospital, while grieving families watched as two bodies were pulled out of an apartment block. "There used to be a building here, and now it's gone," said 45-year-old resident Maria Abramova. She had only just reached her children's room after the air raid alert sounded when explosions rang out, blowing her windows out and "nearly killing" her husband.

stories.title: Kobe-mania and the Irish experiment
stories.summary: The AFL's Irish experiment nearly failed before even it really even began - and it all came down to a split-second decision in the 1987 Victorian Football League preliminary final between Melbourne and Hawthorn. The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. Kept alive by Melbourne’s inefficiency, Gary Buckenara was given one last chance to win it from Hawthorn but from way out, it was a low percentage chance.

stories.title: Arteta offers Arsenal consistency in a world gone maddish
stories.summary: When Mikel Arteta leads Arsenal out at home to Coventry on Friday evening, he will do so as the longest serving manager in the Premier League. Fresh from getting Arsenal over the line to their first league title in more than two decades, Arteta is now the elder statesman of the league after Pep Guardiola decided to call time on his 10 years with Manchester City. The next trick for Arteta is to defend the title and win back-to-back Premier Leagues for the first time in the club's history, surpassing even the achievements of Arsene Wenger. Arsenal go into the season as the heavy favourites. A sense of uncertainty and flux settles in over their rivals, while Arteta’s steady hand, long-term squad building and continued improvement means they’re the team to beat.

stories.title: Debut tries for Flood, Murphy as Leinster defeat Connacht
stories.summary: Debut tries from Stacey Flood and Niamh Murphy helped Leinster to overcome Connacht 36-21 for their opening Vodafone Women's Interprovincial Championship win. Having failed to pick up a point against Munster, this was a must-win game for Leinster at Energia Park, and they prevailed thanks to closing scores from Maggie Boylan and replacement Murphy. Craig Hansberry's young Connacht side led early on, and twice closed the gap to three points, but they are now a point behind second-placed Leinster, in the table, heading into the final round. Leinster's improved performance in front of their home support had them 17-14 ahead at half-time, with Boylan, Hannah Wilson, and Emma Tilly all touching down.

stories.title: Something for the Weekend: The Jimmy Cake's cultural picks
stories.summary: To celebrate the 25th anniversary of their seminal debut album, Brains, The Jimmy Cake will play the album in full - in their first concert in just under a decade at the National Concert Hall this November. The band formed in Dublin in the late 1990s and Brains announced their arrival proper. As a nine-piece blending accordion, clarinet, saxophone, glockenspiel, trumpet and DIY percussion around the core of guitars, bass and drums they went on to release lauded efforts such as 2002’s Dublin Gone. Everybody Dead and 2008’s Spectre and Crown before later albums Master (2015) and Tough Love (2017). Parallel to his involvement with The Jimmy Cake, pianist, synthesist, graphic designer and label manager Paul G Smyth has also set himself apart as a singular voice in Europe’s vigorous improvised music scene, working with luminaries such as Derek Bailey, Evan Parker, Peter Brötzmann and Keiji Haino. I’m being quietly haunted by a film from 2019 called I’m No Longer Here. Written and directed by Fernando Frías de la Parra, it follows an exiled Mexican teenager obsessed with slowed-down cumbia music struggling to adapt in New York after fleeing cartel violence. There’s something unspoken in it that has held me since and I don’t know what it is. "I think I know what it is," my wife said recently as she left the room. That’s helpful, isn’t it?

stories.summary: Claddagh Records is set to release a posthumous spoken-word album by the late broadcaster and writer Manchán Magan. Slí na Samhlaíochta (The Way of Imagination) is out this October and will feature musical contributions from Simon O'Reilly, Myles O’Reilly, Branwen Kavanagh, and Crash Ensemble. Slí na Samhlaíochta came about when the album’s artistic director Simon O’Reilly was working on the Hedge School Festival in Doolin, a small Winter festival in the West of Ireland, in 2023. Manchán Magan had been invited to the Hedge School to perform the closing act, a spoken-word piece that he had been working on, based on the concept of Tír na nÓg – the 'Otherworld’ or ‘An Saol Eile’.

You'll no doubt have seen versions of it: the dewy skin, the glossy blush, the barely there mascara and impeccably groomed brows, all topped off with a shiny slicked-back bun.

stories.title: SF writes to Martin to recall Dáil early over excise cuts
stories.summary: Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald has written to Taoiseach Micheál Martin asking him to recall the Dáil next week so it can vote to delay the first stage of the planned fuel excise duty cuts reversal due on 1 September. Ms McDonald has also called for any further changes to the existing excise duty rate on petrol and diesel to be delayed until after October's budget. The demands have been made in a letter to Mr Martin overnight, which is likely to further ratchet up pressure on Government amid growing debate on whether the planned excise duty cuts reversals should take place. Ongoing uncertainty abroad and protests at home led to the coalition in April agreeing to a cut of 32 cent on a litre of diesel and 27 cent on a litre of petrol.

stories.summary: A man accused of carrying out an arson attack at a Dublin mosque and putting lives at risk has been sent forward for trial. Saeid Khosroabadi, 41, of Seville Place, Dublin 1, was arrested following a fire at the doorway of the Faizan E Madinah Mosque on Talbot Street, in the north inner city, just before 3.30pm on 29 June. Mr Khosroabadi, an Iranian national, was originally charged with committing arson, causing criminal damage at the mosque. Last week, he was held further by Cloverhill District Court after Garda Shane Costello brought an additional charge for endangering life in connection with the blaze.

stories.title: Oil hits 3-week high on Middle East supply concerns
stories.summary: Oil prices climbed to three-week highs today, driven by concerns that the impasse in the Iran war will continue to disrupt supply from the key Middle Eastern producing region. Brent crude futures for October delivery rose $2.44, or 2.7%, to $94.06 a barrel this morning, before $93.48 by evening time. Meanwhile US West Texas Intermediate crude futures for September added $1.84 to $87.67 a barrel, fallen back to $86.47 this evening. Both Brent and WTI benchmarks hit their highest since July 24 and gained for a fifth session in a row. The September WTI contract expires later today. "Tensions in the Middle East remain high, leaving room for further supply disruptions," said UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo. "Lower oil exports from the Middle East are once again tightening the oil market."

stories.title: EU countries, UK call on Israel to halt E1 West Bank plan
stories.summary: France, Italy, Britain and Germany piled on mounting international condemnation of a major settlement project in the occupied West Bank, after Israeli authorities opened bidding for more than 1,200 homes in the area. The E1 plan was green-lit by Israel last year and would further separate east Jerusalem, occupied and annexed by Israel and predominantly inhabited by Palestinians, from the West Bank. "At a time of grave instability in the West Bank with unprecedented levels of violence by settlers against civilians, and serious restrictions on the Palestinian economy, this decision is even more concerning," the joint statement from Paris, Rome, Berlin and London said. "We urge the Government of Israel to retract these plans immediately and end its expansion of settlements in the West Bank," it added, warning businesses against bidding for the construction tenders at risk of "involving themselves in serious breaches of international law".

stories.title: People encouraged to 'enjoy the city' on Culture Night
stories.summary: There will be more than 300 free events taking place across Dublin city next month as part of the capital's Culture Night. The annual event is taking place on 18 September and to mark its 21st year, Culture Night will be expanding its outdoor programming, with more street parties and a variety of performances planned across the capital. For the first time, performances will extend onto North Earl Street, with a series of events and an open-air concert. Across the city, people can expect everything from tango and trad music to painting, poetry, and pole dancing. Also museums, galleries, heritage sites, artists' studios, and independent venues will open their doors to the public, after hours, for the night.

stories.title: Spa Weekend: one star for this Bridesmaids knock-off
stories.summary: The makers of the Hangover movies and Bad Moms try to create the magic and chemistry of Bridesmaids by plonking four old girlfriends in an upscale Palm Springs spa retreat in this madcap but ultimately misfiring comedy. Fine comedic actors - Leslie Mann as the uptight Jane, Michelle Buteau as badass Coco, Isla Fisher as trainwreck Mel, and Anna Faris as workaholic Sophie - gather for a girls behaving badly romp that lays on the bad taste gags as thick as a collagen face mask as they try to recapture the spirit of 2011 at the box office. Thing is the firecracker Mel is the one that nobody likes in the friend group, an unwelcome interloper from the distant past who turns up uninvited, unwanted and unannounced to cause merry mayhem amid the potted plants and Zen gardens. Before you can say "namaste", wellness turns to badness and sessions of goat yoga, guided meditation, and restorative mud baths descend into slapstick farce, pratfalls. and lessons learnt about the true value of friendship. In a wafer thin script exploding with F bombs, cliches collide and thoroughly dated bad taste jokes refuse to land. The gung-ho cast do their best with very poor material and at least they were having a good time.

stories.title: 8 things to do post-breakup to help you get through it
stories.summary: Breakups suck. Whether you're the one leaving or the one being left, they’re messy. While traditional face-to-face breakups seem to be a thing of the past, unfortunately, most of us are stuck on the receiving end of uncreative tropes like ghosting or just being treated terribly until we take the hint. On the plus side, I find there’s something truly magical in that post-breakup clarity. The absolute motivation I feel in the depths of heartbreak needs to be bottled and sold: "Eau du Spite" by Tara, now available in all good pharmacies. stories.title: Irish excise on alcohol second highest in Europe - study
stories.summary: Irish consumers pay the second highest excise duty on alcohol in Europe, according to new research. The research from Dublin City University economist Anthony Foley, commissioned by the Drinks Industry Group of Ireland (DIGI), shows that Ireland comes only behind Finland when it comes to excise levies on alcohol. When broken down by type of alcoholic drink, excise on wine in Ireland is the second highest in the EU and UK, also behind Finland, while excise on beer and spirits is the third highest, behind Finland and Sweden. A pint of beer purchased in a pub here attracts an excise duty of €0.55 compared to just €0.05 in Spain and Germany.

stories.title: 79% of adults interested in new savings scheme - research
stories.summary: The vast majority of adults in Ireland (79%) are interested in investing in the Government's new planned Savings and Investment Account, research from the Banking & Payments Federation Ireland (BPFI) suggests. Tánaiste and Minister for Finance Simon Harris is expected to announce details of the State-backed scheme in October's Budget, which is due to be up and running next year. It will likely include a single flat rate of tax on any savings invested, with the Government hoping the planned favourable tax terms will entice savers who currently have around €170 billion on deposit to invest. According to the BPFI survey, almost half of adults (48%) are aware of the scheme, although this drops to 25% of younger adults aged 18-34.

In July, the EU approved its most ⁠recent sanctions package against Russia over its war in Ukraine, imposing curbs on the country's banking sector and cryptocurrency networks. The bloc has adopted 21 rounds of sanctions against Russia since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. stories.title: Numbers at work up by 0.8% to 2.8 million in Q2 - CSO
stories.summary: Employment in Ireland has increased by 0.8% to more than 2.8 million, driven by an increase in older age groups and citizens from across the world coming to work here, according to the Central Statistics Office's latest Labour Force Survey. The statistics for the second quarter relate to the second three months of this year. The CSO figures show that the employment rate in Ireland for those aged 15 to 64 is currently 74.3%, down 0.4 percentage points on the year. The unemployment rate was 5.1%, up 0.3 percentage points compared to the same period last year.

stories.title: Hawkshaw proud of Ireland efforts after Belgian defeat
stories.summary: Ireland captain Sarah Hawkshaw expressed pride in her team-mates despite their Women's Hockey World Cup dream being dashed by hosts Belgium on Thursday. Gareth Grundie's side put in a gutsy display in the Belfius Hockey Arena but fell to a 2-1 defeat. The result means Ireland will not advance further in the competition but will go through the consolation of the classification rounds. "You get sick of saying we're that close when we're (getting) 2-1 scorelines against top three teams in the world," she said.

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.
